title: Pulmonary Involvement in Children With Systemic JIA
off: Clinical Characteristics of Pulmonary Involvement in Children With Systemic Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis
summary: This cross-sectional study aims to describe the clinical characteristics of pulmonary involvement in children with systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis.
desc:
Systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis is an autoinflammatory disease that can be associated with severe lung disease. Systemic JIA-associated lung disease may present with chronic cough, dyspnea, and characteristic radiographic findings.

This observational study will evaluate clinical, laboratory, and radiographic features of lung involvement in children aged 16 years or younger diagnosed with systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis according to ILAR criteria at Assiut University Children's Hospital.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Children with systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis fulfilling ILAR classification criteria
* Age 16 years or younger
* Written informed consent from parent or legal guardian

Exclusion Criteria:

* \- Other subtypes of juvenile idiopathic arthritis
* Pre-existing chronic lung disease unrelated to systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis
* Overlapping connective tissue disease or distinct autoinflammatory syndrome other than systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis
* Age greater than 16 years

arms.l: Children with Systemic Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis
arms.d: Children aged 16 years or younger with systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis undergoing clinical and radiographic assessment for pulmonary involvement.
